advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Point REBAR_ROOT and `git init` at the SAME directory in run_quickstart (e.g. `git init` inside `.rebar-store`, or set REBAR_ROOT to `workdir`), so `rebar init` targets the initialized git repo.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_init.py:47-49 `root = os.environ.get("REBAR_ROOT")` … `if not root: root = _git_toplevel()` — REBAR_ROOT wins over cwd git toplevel
src/rebar/_commands/init.py:358 `cp = _git(repo, "worktree", "add", "--orphan", "-b", branch, tracker)` with repo == REBAR_ROOT (a non-git dir) → non-zero → init returns 1
advisory.finding: run_quickstart runs `git init` in `workdir` but sets REBAR_ROOT to `workdir/.rebar-store`; since `rebar init` resolves the repo from REBAR_ROOT (which takes precedence over the git toplevel), it operates on `.rebar-store` — a non-existent, non-git directory — so `git worktree add --orphan` fails and `rebar init` exits non-zero, failing the entire quickstart block under `bash -euo pipefail` even for a correct README.
scenarios: Running the gate in CI against the real README
advisory.suggested_fix: Either drop the REBAR_ROOT override and rely on cwd=workdir (the git repo just inited), or run `git init` in `os.path.join(workdir, '.rebar-store')` and point REBAR_ROOT there — the two must reference one git repo.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the README quickstart gate against a clean installed rebar (e.g. a separate pipx/pip install) rather than only the editable dev install, per ticket 0435 AC #2.
evidence: ticket 0435 AC: "The job runs against an installed rebar (not just `src` on `PYTHONPATH`), catching packaging/entry-point regressions too."
advisory.finding: The ticket AC requires the gate to run against an INSTALLED rebar (clean pipx/pip install) to also catch packaging/entry-point regressions, but both wired CI steps run in jobs that install rebar editable via `pip install -e '.[dev]'` (src on PYTHONPATH), so packaging/entry-point regressions are not exercised.
scenarios: A packaging/entry-point regression (missing console_script, missing package data) that an editable install masks

evidence: Test file only exercises the bad-subcommand class: test_check_readme_quickstart.py:115 `'rebar init\nrebar session-log "note"\n',  # invalid: missing the `append` verb`
CI comment states both classes are in scope: test.yml:275 `# A wrong command *printed* in the README (e.g. a bad subcommand or a stale`
Ticket acceptance criterion: 'a wrong command printed in the README — e.g. session-log missing its append verb, or a disconnected hard-coded id — is demonstrably caught'
ABSENCE: no test in tests/scripts/test_check_readme_quickstart.py writes a README quickstart with a hard-coded ticket id and asserts main() exits non-zero
Source branch untested: check_readme_quickstart.py:111 `readme = args.readme if args.readme is not None else DEFAULT_README`
Both E2E tests use the default path: test_check_readme_quickstart.py:117 `monkeypatch.setattr(chk, "DEFAULT_README", readme, raising=False)` then `chk.main([])`
Docstring documents the untested usage: check_readme_quickstart.py:16 `python scripts/check_readme_quickstart.py --readme P # run against P`
ABSENCE: no test invokes chk.main(["--readme", str(path)])
advisory.finding: The 'stale/disconnected hard-coded id' README-text defect class — explicitly named in the ticket acceptance criteria and in the CI step comment ('a stale hard-coded id') as a behavior this gate must catch — has no regression test. The E2E failure test only covers a bad subcommand (session-log missing `append`).
merged_from: The main() `--readme` CLI argument branch is never exercised. All main() tests call main([]) and monkeypatch DEFAULT_README, so the documented `--readme P` path (args.readme is not None) has no coverage.
scenarios: README quickstart is edited to use a literal hard-coded ticket id instead of the $tid capture pipeline; the gate should fail but no test proves it does
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test mirroring test_main_fails_on_broken_quickstart_command that writes a quickstart block like `rebar init\nrebar claim 0000-dead-beef-0000 --assignee alice\n` (a disconnected hard-coded id) and asserts chk.main([]) != 0.
